title: Pipeline Registers with Stall and Flush
constraints: Three stages S1 → S2 → S3, each holding (valid, data). The outputs are S3's contents.
Normal edge: S3 ← S2, S2 ← S1, S1 ← (in_valid, in_data).
`stall = 1`: every stage holds and the input is not accepted.
`flush = 1` (priority over stall): S3 ← S2 (the oldest instruction still completes), while S2 and S1 become invalid bubbles and the input is dropped.
Synchronous reset (priority over everything) clears all valid bits. `out_data` is don't-care when `out_valid = 0`. Must be synthesizable.
hints: Keep a valid bit and a data register per stage, updated in one clocked block.
Order the if-chain by priority: rst, then flush, then stall, then normal shifting.
A flush is what a branch misprediction does to the younger instructions behind the branch.

examples.title: flow
examples.input: in = A, B, C, … with in_valid = 1
examples.expected: out = A three edges after it entered, then B, C, …

examples.title: stall
examples.expected: out holds, nothing is lost, flow resumes

examples.title: flush
examples.input: flush while A (S3), B (S2), C (S1) are in flight
examples.expected: B comes out next, then two invalid cycles
